answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when a challenge proves collusion or fabricated work. Because one operator creating a hundred hollow identities must fund a hundred locks, Sybil attacks become capital-intensive rather than free; the stake also makes honest participants wary of lending credentials. A saffron badge or velvet-sounding profile earns no exemption: only bonded identities gain influence, and the attacker risks losing the funds.
